set.body:
Journey 4 of docs/plan.md.

Done when
A frozen study passes a readiness checklist, leaves as a validated BIDS package, receives a DOI from an established repository and is found by cohort query in a Neurobagel node. OPEN5 is the acceptance rehearsal.

Design decisions
- Open means publish outward. Sanctity prepares, verifies and records the publication. An established repository hosts the public copy and mints the DOI. Sanctity serves no anonymous users, so no internet-facing review is needed for the MVP.
- The descriptive fields live in the dataset itself (dataset_description.json, README, LICENSE, participants.json), so the published copy describes itself and edits go through normal review.
- Publishing tools live in tools/publish (Python) and use the HTTP API. The default service distribution has no Neurobagel dependency.
- The rehearsal uses Zenodo's sandbox, which issues test DOIs and publishes nothing. OpenNeuro has no sandbox, so the proposed real destination is exercised only when the owner names a real study in OPEN0 and confirms at the deposit step.
- Publication state lives in the dataset. Readiness attestations and the publication record are small files under sourcedata/sanctity/, added through normal corrections and left out of the public package. There are no new server tables.
- Publication control (approval bound to target generations, verified withdrawal) and outbound federation search are parked as NB02 and NB04.

What exists
Archive deposit with DataCite-style fields. An 18 November probe showed that the bagel command-line tool turns a participants table, an annotated dictionary and an imaging table into Neurobagel JSON-LD without image bytes.

Order
OPEN0 (owner) runs alongside the build. OPEN1 follows the study page (SEE4). OPEN2 follows SHARE2 and OPEN1. OPEN3 can start now. OPEN4 follows OPEN3. OPEN5 closes the journey.
set.title: OPEN: Publish a frozen study as open and FAIR
